checklist.step: Confirm the OFAC Sanctions Compliance Officer designation is current
actions: Pull the current org chart and confirm the Financial Crime AML Officer holds the SCO mandate with authority, autonomy and direct access to the Board Risk Committee, per the OFAC Framework's Management Commitment pillar.
Confirm the SCO role sits outside any business line that could pressure a blocking or licensing decision (sales, underwriting, distribution).
Where the seat is vacant or the incumbent has changed, open a governance-gap exception in the regulatory filing/issue tracker the same day.
Record the current SCO name, start date and reporting line in the governance register.
checklist.done: the governance register shows a named, independent SCO with a documented direct line to the Risk Committee, or an open exception with a target-fill date.

checklist.step: Refresh the Sanctions Compliance Program Governance Charter annually
actions: Pull the prior-year charter from the board portal document library and redline it against the current OFAC Framework for Compliance Commitments and 31 CFR 501.603-501.604.
Update the escalation thresholds, committee membership list and SCO authority/autonomy language to reflect any organizational change in the year.
Route the redline to General Counsel for legal sufficiency review before it goes to committee.
Upload the clean and redlined versions to the board portal charter folder, version-stamped.
checklist.done: a redlined and clean charter draft is in the board portal, cleared by General Counsel, ahead of the next Risk Committee cycle.

checklist.step: Schedule the standing quarterly Risk Committee sanctions agenda item
actions: In the board portal, open the Risk Committee's recurring meeting series and confirm 'Sanctions Compliance Program' is a standing agenda line.
Set the invite distribution list to the Risk Committee, the SCO and the Head of Compliance.
Attach the standing agenda template requiring: SCO attestation, screening-program KPIs, exception log summary, training completion rate.
Confirm the meeting date sits inside the current quarter and no more than 100 days after the prior sanctions-agenda session.
checklist.done: the quarter's Risk Committee meeting carries a confirmed sanctions agenda item with the correct distribution list.

checklist.step: Assemble the board pack from program KPIs
actions: In the sanctions screening system, export the quarter's alert volume, true-match count, false-positive rate and average alert-disposition time from the case management dashboard.
Pull the current exception log extract from the regulatory filing/issue tracker and the training completion rate for covered employees and producers.
Draft the SCO written attestation confirming the program remains adequately resourced and independent.
Send the package to the Corporate Secretary at least 5 business days before the meeting.
checklist.done: the board pack contains screening KPIs, the exception summary, training completion and a signed SCO attestation, delivered on time.

checklist.step: Distribute the board pack ahead of the meeting
actions: Upload the assembled pack to the board portal meeting folder.
Publish it to Risk Committee members at least 5 business days ahead of the session per the committee's standing notice requirement.
Confirm read-receipts in the portal and follow up individually with any member who has not opened the pack 2 business days before the meeting.
checklist.done: every Risk Committee member has portal access to the pack at least 5 business days before the meeting, with read confirmation logged.

checklist.step: Attend the Risk Committee session and minute the sanctions item
actions: Capture attendance, the SCO's verbal attestation, questions raised and any directed follow-up actions verbatim in the minute draft.
Record any dissent or condition attached to approval of the program status.
Note the vote or consensus outcome on continued SCO authority and program adequacy.
checklist.done: a complete draft minute exists covering attendance, attestation, discussion and outcome for the sanctions agenda item.

checklist.step: Circulate and finalize the minutes
actions: Send the draft minute to the Committee Chair for review within 3 business days of the meeting.
Incorporate the Chair's corrections and recirculate to the full committee for approval at the next session or by written consent.
Stamp the minute 'Approved' with the approval date once confirmed.
checklist.done: the minute is Chair-reviewed and committee-approved, with the approval date recorded.

checklist.step: File the approved charter and minutes in the evidence repository
actions: Upload the approved minute and, if refreshed this cycle, the newly approved charter to the compliance evidence repository under the Sanctions Governance folder.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Cross-reference the repository record id back into the board portal meeting entry.
checklist.done: the approved artifacts are in the evidence repository, labelled for 5-year retention and cross-referenced to the board portal.

checklist.step: Renew the SCO authority-and-autonomy attestation
actions: Prepare the annual written attestation confirming the SCO has sufficient authority, autonomy, resources and access to senior management and the Board.
Route it for CEO countersignature.
File the countersigned attestation alongside the charter in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a CEO-countersigned SCO authority-and-autonomy attestation exists for the current year.

checklist.step: Track and escalate governance incidents within the 10-business-day SLA
actions: Log any sanctions-governance incident (missed session, vacant seat, breached independence) in the tracker the day it is identified.
Set the escalation-to-Board SLA field to 10 business days from the log date.
Notify the Head of Compliance and the Board Governance Lead immediately for any incident touching SCO independence.
checklist.done: every governance incident is logged with a 10-business-day escalation SLA and the required notifications sent.

checklist.step: Maintain the Risk Committee membership roster
actions: Update the roster on any appointment, resignation or term expiry.
Confirm the incoming member has no conflicting business-line role that would compromise sanctions oversight independence.
Publish the updated roster to the board portal governance section.
checklist.done: the published roster matches the current committee membership with no unresolved independence conflict.

checklist.step: Verify SCO independence from pressured business decisions
actions: Review the quarter's blocking, rejection and license-use decisions for any instance where a business-line executive overrode or pressured the SCO's call.
Interview the SCO on any escalation that was resisted or delayed by the business.
Record the finding in the quarterly board pack, positive or negative.
checklist.done: the quarter's independence review is documented, with any override instance escalated to the Board.

checklist.step: Deliver the annual Board sanctions-governance briefing
actions: Present a rollup of the year's alert volumes, blocked/rejected transaction counts, training completion and any enforcement-relevant industry developments to the full Board.
Walk through any open governance exceptions and their remediation status.
Capture Board questions and directed actions in the minute.
checklist.done: the full Board has received and minuted the annual sanctions-governance briefing.

checklist.step: Log and disposition any open governance exceptions
actions: Review all open governance exceptions in the tracker each quarter.
Confirm each has an owner, root cause and target date; escalate any exception past its target date to the Board Governance Lead.
Close exceptions only on documented remediation evidence.
checklist.done: every open governance exception carries an owner, root cause and current status, with overdue items escalated.

checklist.step: Archive superseded charter and policy versions
actions: Move prior charter versions to the archived-versions folder in the compliance evidence repository once a new version is approved.
Confirm the version history remains traceable (who approved, when, what changed).
Verify the current charter is the only version marked 'Active' in the repository index.
checklist.done: only the current charter is marked Active and all superseded versions are archived with a traceable history.

testing.step: Build the population of governance events in scope
actions: Extract from the board portal every Risk Committee meeting held in the test period and confirm which carried the standing sanctions agenda item.
Pull the charter version history and every SCO authority-autonomy attestation on file for the period.
Reconcile the extracted meeting count to the committee's published annual calendar and resolve any gap before sampling.
testing.done: the population of sanctions-agenda meetings, charter versions and attestations is complete and reconciled to the published calendar.

testing.step: Confirm SCO designation continuity across the period
actions: Build a timeline of who held the SCO seat for every day in the test period from HR and governance records.
Identify any gap exceeding 30 days and confirm it was logged as a governance exception with escalation.
Flag any period where the SCO reported into a business-line executive rather than the Risk Committee.
testing.done: the SCO-continuity timeline is built and every gap or independence break is matched to a logged, escalated exception.

testing.step: Select the sample of committee sessions and charter cycles
actions: Take 100% of Risk Committee sessions in the test period given the low annual volume.
Take the current and prior charter version for detailed redline review.
Record the sample composition and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all sessions in the period plus the current and prior charter versions, logged in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-verify the board pack notice period and content for each sampled session
actions: In the board portal, check the publish timestamp of the pack against the meeting date for each sampled session and confirm at least 5 business days' notice.
Confirm the pack contained screening KPIs, the exception summary, training completion and a signed SCO attestation.
Screenshot the portal publish log into the workpaper as evidence of timely distribution.
testing.done: every sampled session shows a timely, complete board pack with captured evidence of the publish timestamp.

testing.step: Independently re-read the charter against current OFAC guidance
actions: Re-read the current charter clause by clause against the OFAC Framework for Compliance Commitments and 31 CFR 501.603-501.604 without reference to the prior sign-off.
Note any clause that no longer reflects current guidance or organizational structure.
Log any gap as a finding requiring charter amendment at the next cycle.
testing.done: an independent legal re-read of the charter is documented, with any gap logged as a finding.

testing.step: Trace minutes to Chair approval and repository filing
actions: For each sampled session, confirm the minute shows Chair review within 3 business days and committee approval at or before the next session.
Confirm the approved minute is filed in the compliance evidence repository under the 5-year retention label.
Flag any minute missing Chair sign-off or repository filing as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled minute traces to a dated Chair approval and a retention-labelled repository record, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test the independence review for pressured decisions
actions: Pull the quarter's blocked/rejected transaction and license-use decision log and independently check for any instance of a documented override or delay by a business-line executive.
Interview the SCO directly, separate from the Head of Compliance's own quarterly review, and compare findings.
Any undisclosed override found by the auditor that was not in the board pack is an automatic exception.
testing.done: an independent override check is complete and reconciled against the Head of Compliance's own finding, with any gap logged.

testing.step: Recompute the 10-business-day escalation SLA on sampled incidents
actions: Pull every governance incident logged in the tracker during the period.
Recompute business days from log date to Board escalation date for each and compare to the 10-business-day SLA.
Any incident escalated late, or not escalated at all, is a reportable exception.
testing.done: every logged incident's escalation timing is recomputed and compared to the 10-business-day SLA, with breaches logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception with the meeting/attestation id, what was missed and the governance impact.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry any open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and draft the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective).
Have the Internal Auditor, independent of the governance process, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any open exception to the Risk Committee at its next session and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Open the annual blocked-property reporting cycle
actions: Each June, create the annual milestone in the regulatory filing/issue tracker for the September 30 OFAC Annual Report of Blocked Property.
Set T-60, T-30 and T-10 day reminders addressed to the Financial Crime AML Officer and General Counsel.
Confirm the prior year's filing confirmation is on file as the reference baseline.
checklist.done: the September 30 milestone with staged reminders exists in the tracker for the current cycle.

checklist.step: Extract the current blocked-property register
actions: In the sanctions screening system case management module, filter cases with disposition 'Blocked' that remain blocked as of June 30.
For each, pull the SDN identifier, blocking date, property description, estimated value and the sanctions program cited.
Reconcile the count against the register carried forward from the prior year's report plus any new blocks and minus any unblocks recorded during the year.
Flag any unreconciled item to the Sanctions Analyst for investigation before compiling the report.
checklist.done: the blocked-property register is extracted and reconciled to the prior year plus current-year movements with no unresolved items.

checklist.step: Draft the OFAC Annual Report of Blocked Property
actions: Complete the annual report using the reconciled register, entering each blocked item's identifying data, value and program.
Cross-check every SDN identifier against the current SDN List to confirm the listing is still active.
Route the draft to General Counsel for review against 31 CFR 501.603(b)(2) content requirements before submission.
checklist.done: the draft annual report is complete, every listing is confirmed active, and General Counsel has reviewed it.

checklist.step: Submit the annual report by September 30
actions: Submit the finalized annual report through OFAC's designated reporting channel on or before September 30.
Retain the submission confirmation (confirmation number or delivery receipt) the same day.
Update the regulatory filing/issue tracker milestone to 'Filed' with the confirmation reference attached.
checklist.done: the annual report is filed by September 30 with a retained confirmation and the tracker milestone closed.

checklist.step: File the annual report and confirmation in the evidence repository
actions: Upload the filed report and the submission confirmation to the compliance evidence repository under the current filing year.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Link the repository record id to the tracker milestone.
checklist.done: the filed report and confirmation are archived, retention-labelled, and cross-referenced to the tracker.

checklist.step: Open a rejected-transaction reporting case on each qualifying event
actions: On any transaction rejected due to a sanctions nexus that does not result in a block, open a case in the sanctions screening system tagged 'Rejected Transaction Report Required'.
Record the rejection date, party identifiers, transaction type and the sanctions basis.
Start the 10-business-day countdown timer in the regulatory filing/issue tracker from the rejection date.
checklist.done: a tagged case with a running 10-business-day timer exists for every qualifying rejected transaction the same day it occurs.

checklist.step: Draft and route the rejected-transaction report
actions: Complete the rejected-transaction report from the case data, citing the specific sanctions program and legal basis for rejection.
Route to General Counsel for review within 3 business days of the rejection date, leaving a buffer inside the 10-business-day window.
Incorporate any General Counsel edits and finalize.
checklist.done: the rejected-transaction report is drafted and General Counsel-reviewed with at least 5 business days remaining before the deadline.

checklist.step: Submit the rejected-transaction report within 10 business days
actions: Submit the finalized rejected-transaction report through OFAC's designated reporting channel within 10 business days of the rejection event.
Retain the submission confirmation.
Close the sanctions screening system case and stop the tracker countdown timer.
checklist.done: the report is submitted within the 10-business-day window with a retained confirmation, and the case is closed.

checklist.step: Draft the sanctions-program narrative for the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure
actions: Pull the current sanctions governance charter status, SCO designation and the year's blocked/rejected transaction counts from the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Draft the CGAD sanctions-program section describing the compliance structure, oversight cadence and material incidents, if any.
Route the draft narrative to General Counsel for legal sufficiency review.
checklist.done: a draft CGAD sanctions-program narrative exists and has been reviewed by General Counsel.

checklist.step: File the CGAD with the lead state insurance regulator
actions: Assemble the full CGAD, incorporating the sanctions-program narrative alongside the other required governance sections.
Submit the CGAD to the lead state regulator by its statutory due date.
Retain the filed CGAD and any regulator acknowledgment.
checklist.done: the CGAD is filed on time with the lead state regulator, retained with acknowledgment.

checklist.step: Reconcile the year's filings against the tracker
actions: At year end, confirm every rejected-transaction case opened during the year has a matching filed report and closed tracker entry.
Confirm the annual report and CGAD milestones both show 'Filed' status with confirmations attached.
Escalate any unreconciled or missing filing to General Counsel immediately.
checklist.done: every filing obligation for the year reconciles to a filed report with a confirmation on file, with no open gaps.

checklist.step: Assess and self-disclose any late filing
actions: On discovery of a missed September 30 deadline or a rejected-transaction report filed beyond 10 business days, assess materiality and the case for voluntary self-disclosure to OFAC.
Prepare and submit the self-disclosure where warranted, describing the root cause and remediation taken.
Log the self-disclosure decision and outcome in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: any late filing has a documented materiality assessment and, where warranted, a filed self-disclosure with logged outcome.

checklist.step: Update the filings procedure after any regulatory change
actions: Monitor OFAC and NAIC guidance updates affecting the annual report, rejected-transaction reporting, or CGAD content requirements.
Redline the OFAC Governance Filings Procedure to reflect any change.
Route the redlined procedure to General Counsel for approval.
checklist.done: the filings procedure is current with the latest OFAC/NAIC guidance and General Counsel-approved.

checklist.step: Brief the Risk Committee on the year's filings
actions: Summarize the year's annual report, rejected-transaction filings and CGAD sanctions narrative for the next Risk Committee session.
Include any late filing, self-disclosure, or regulator follow-up question.
Capture Committee questions and directed actions in the minute.
checklist.done: the Risk Committee has received and minuted a summary of the year's OFAC governance filings.

checklist.step: Retain and index all filings for the retention period
actions: Confirm every filing (annual report, rejected-transaction reports, CGAD) for the year is indexed in the compliance evidence repository by filing type and date.
Apply the 5-year retention label to each.
Spot-check the repository index for retrievability by filing type.
checklist.done: all of the year's filings are indexed, retention-labelled and retrievable by type in the repository.

testing.step: Build the population of filings and events for the test period
actions: Extract every rejected-transaction case opened, the annual report filing, and the CGAD filing from the tracker for the test period.
Reconcile the rejected-transaction case count to the sanctions screening system's tagged case log.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population of filings is reconciled between the tracker and the sanctions screening system.

testing.step: Reconcile the annual report to the blocked-property register
actions: Independently re-extract the blocked-property register as of the reporting date from the sanctions screening system.
Compare line by line to the filed annual report.
Log any omitted, extra or misstated line as an exception.
testing.done: the filed annual report is independently reconciled to the register with any discrepancy logged.

testing.step: Select the sample of rejected-transaction reports
actions: Take 100% of rejected-transaction reports filed in the test period given typically low volume; if volume exceeds 40, take a random sample of 25 plus all late filings.
Record the population size, sample method and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and its method documented, covering all late filings regardless of random draw.

testing.step: Recompute the 10-business-day deadline for each sampled report
actions: For each sampled case, recompute business days from the rejection date to the actual submission date.
Compare to the 10-business-day standard and flag any breach.
Cross-check the submission date against the retained confirmation, not the drafter's own log.
testing.done: every sampled report's timing is independently recomputed and confirmed against the retained submission confirmation.

testing.step: Verify General Counsel review occurred before each submission
actions: Confirm a dated General Counsel review exists for each sampled rejected-transaction report and the annual report, predating submission.
Flag any report submitted without a documented legal review.
testing.done: every sampled filing traces to a dated pre-submission legal review, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm the CGAD sanctions narrative matches the year's actual program status
actions: Compare the filed CGAD sanctions-program narrative to the actual SCO designation, incident log and blocked/rejected transaction counts for the year.
Flag any material inconsistency or omission.
Confirm the CGAD was filed by its statutory due date.
testing.done: the CGAD narrative is verified consistent with the year's actual program record and timely filed.

testing.step: Trace submission confirmations to the evidence repository
actions: For each sampled filing, confirm the submission confirmation and filed copy are present in the compliance evidence repository under the correct retention label.
Flag any missing or unlabelled artifact.
testing.done: every sampled filing's evidence is present and correctly labelled in the repository, or logged as a gap.

testing.step: Test any self-disclosure decision for completeness
actions: For any late filing identified in the sample, confirm a materiality assessment and self-disclosure decision were documented by General Counsel.
Flag any late filing lacking a documented decision as an exception.
testing.done: every late filing in the sample has a documented materiality assessment and self-disclosure decision, or is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception, describing the filing, what was missed and the regulatory impact.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry any unresolved exception into the next test cycle as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and draft the conclusion.
Have the Internal Auditor, independent of the filings process, sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Open the assessment file on nomination

Capture full legal name, prior names/aliases, date of birth, nationality and known business affiliations from the nomination packet.
Set the HRIS workflow status to 'Assessment In Progress', which blocks the downstream appointment-ratification task.
checklist.done: an HRIS assessment record exists for the candidate with the ratification task blocked pending completion.

checklist.step: Run the sanctions and adverse-media screen

Run the screen against OFAC's SDN List, Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List and Consolidated Sanctions List, plus adverse-media sources.
Review any potential match for name-only false positives using date of birth, nationality and known affiliations.
Document the disposition (clear / true match / needs escalation) in the case record.
checklist.done: a documented sanctions and adverse-media screening disposition exists for the candidate.

checklist.step: Escalate any true or unresolved sanctions match immediately
actions: On any true match or unresolved potential match, notify General Counsel and the Head of Compliance within 1 business day.
Halt the appointment process pending resolution.
Document the escalation and the resolution path in the case record.
checklist.done: any true or unresolved match is escalated within 1 business day with the appointment halted pending resolution.

checklist.step: Commission the background and financial-crime check
actions: Order a criminal-history, civil-litigation and regulatory-action background check from the approved vendor for the candidate's jurisdictions of residence and citizenship.
Request disclosure of any prior regulatory sanction, bar or license revocation.
Log the check's order date and expected turnaround in the HRIS record.
checklist.done: a background and financial-crime check is commissioned and logged for the candidate.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate's affiliation and conflicts disclosure
actions: Send the candidate the officer/director disclosure form covering external directorships, ownership interests, and any foreign-government or sanctioned-jurisdiction affiliation.
Review the completed form for any affiliation that could create a sanctions exposure or conflict of interest.
Route any flagged affiliation to General Counsel for review.
checklist.done: a completed disclosure form is on file and any flagged affiliation is routed for legal review.

checklist.step: Legal review of the full assessment file
actions: Review the sanctions screening disposition, background check results and disclosure form together.
Assess whether any finding disqualifies the candidate or requires a mitigation condition (recusal, divestiture).
Record the legal conclusion and any condition in the assessment file.
checklist.done: General Counsel has recorded a documented conclusion on the candidate's fitness, with any condition specified.

checklist.step: Route the assessment for Board or Nominating Committee ratification
actions: Attach the completed assessment file, legal conclusion and any conditions to the nomination package in the board portal.
Present the nomination for ratification at the next Board or Nominating Committee session.
Record the ratification vote and any imposed condition in the minute.
checklist.done: the nomination is ratified (or declined) by the Board with the assessment file attached and the vote minuted.

checklist.step: Close and file the completed assessment
actions: Set the HRIS workflow status to 'Assessment Complete' upon ratification, unblocking the appointment record.
Upload the full assessment file to the compliance evidence repository under the individual's officer/director record.
Apply the 5-year-post-departure retention label.
checklist.done: the assessment is filed in the evidence repository with the correct retention label and the HRIS record shows Complete.

checklist.step: Schedule the annual re-screening for sitting officers and directors
actions: Confirm the HRIS anniversary-date reminder is active for every sitting officer and director.
On the reminder date, open a re-screening case and re-run the sanctions and adverse-media screen.
Re-collect the affiliation disclosure to capture any change since the last assessment.
checklist.done: every sitting officer and director has an annual re-screening triggered and completed on schedule.

checklist.step: Document any condition or mitigation imposed
actions: Where a condition (recusal from certain votes, divestiture of a flagged interest) was imposed, document the condition's terms and monitoring owner.
Set a follow-up date to confirm the condition has been satisfied.
Record satisfaction or ongoing status in the assessment file.
checklist.done: any imposed condition has documented terms, a monitoring owner and a tracked satisfaction status.

checklist.step: Track departures and update sanctions monitoring accordingly
actions: On any officer or director departure, update the HRIS record and notify the Sanctions Analyst to remove the individual from ongoing periodic screening once the retention clock starts.
Confirm the departure date is recorded to anchor the 5-year retention period.
checklist.done: departures are recorded promptly and periodic screening is updated to reflect current officers and directors only.

checklist.step: Report assessment status to the Risk Committee
actions: Prepare a rollup of the year's new appointments, completed re-screenings and any open escalation for the Risk Committee.
Present alongside the sanctions governance briefing.
Capture Committee feedback in the minute.
checklist.done: the Risk Committee has received a rollup of the year's fitness-and-propriety activity.

checklist.step: Log any exception in the assessment process
actions: Log any instance where an appointment proceeded without a completed screening, or a re-screening was missed past its due date.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Escalate any unresolved exception past 30 days to General Counsel.
checklist.done: every process exception is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date, with overdue items escalated.

checklist.step: Update the assessment procedure after any regulatory change
actions: Monitor OFAC list-screening guidance and NAIC director/officer fitness standards for changes.
Redline the Officer and Director Fitness-and-Propriety Assessment Procedure accordingly.
Route the redline to the Chief HR Officer for co-approval.
checklist.done: the assessment procedure reflects current OFAC and NAIC guidance and carries a current co-approval.

checklist.step: Retain and index completed assessments
actions: Confirm every completed assessment for the year is indexed in the compliance evidence repository by individual name and appointment date.
Spot-check retrievability of a sample record.
Confirm departed individuals' records remain retrievable through their retention window.
checklist.done: all assessments for the year are indexed and retrievable, including those of departed individuals within their retention window.

testing.step: Build the population of appointments and re-screenings
actions: Extract every new officer/director appointment and every annual re-screening due or completed in the test period from the HRIS governance module.
Reconcile the extract to the Board/Committee ratification minutes for the period.
Resolve any unreconciled item before sampling.
testing.done: the population of appointments and re-screenings is reconciled to Board ratification records.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of new appointments in the test period.
Take a random sample of 15 annual re-screenings from the sitting officer/director population, or 100% if fewer than 15 are due.
Record the population size, method and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn covering all new appointments and a representative re-screening set, documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the sanctions screen for each sampled individual
actions: Independently re-run the sanctions and adverse-media screen for each sampled individual using their name, aliases and date of birth as recorded.
Compare the auditor's disposition to the recorded disposition in the case file.
Any discrepancy, including an unresolved potential match, is a finding requiring immediate escalation.
testing.done: each sampled individual has an independently re-performed screening result reconciled against the recorded disposition.

testing.step: Verify appointment ratification did not precede assessment completion
actions: For each sampled new appointment, compare the HRIS 'Assessment Complete' timestamp to the board portal ratification vote date.
Flag any appointment ratified before the assessment was marked complete.
Confirm the assessment file was attached to the board portal nomination package presented for the vote.
testing.done: every sampled appointment's ratification date is confirmed to follow assessment completion, with the file attached to the board record.

testing.step: Verify background check completeness and legal review
actions: Confirm a background/financial-crime check result and a dated General Counsel legal-review conclusion exist for each sampled individual.
Confirm any imposed condition has a documented monitoring owner and current status.
Flag any missing element as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled file shows a completed background check, a legal-review conclusion, and any condition's tracked status, or is flagged.

testing.step: Verify disclosure form completeness and follow-through
actions: Confirm each sampled individual's affiliation and conflicts disclosure form is on file and dated before ratification.
Re-check any disclosed affiliation against the sanctions screening result to confirm it was properly assessed.
Flag any disclosure that was not followed up as required.
testing.done: every sampled disclosure form is verified on file, timely, and properly cross-checked against the sanctions screen.

testing.step: Test the annual re-screening cadence
actions: For each sampled sitting officer/director, confirm the re-screening occurred within 12 months of the prior screening date per the HRIS anniversary reminder.
Flag any re-screening more than 30 days overdue against its anniversary date.
testing.done: every sampled re-screening's timing is checked against the 12-month cadence, with overdue items flagged.

testing.step: Trace assessment records to the evidence repository
actions: Confirm each sampled assessment file is present in the compliance evidence repository under the correct individual and retention label.
Confirm departed individuals sampled remain retrievable within their post-departure retention window.
Flag any missing or mislabelled record.
testing.done: every sampled assessment record is confirmed present and correctly labelled in the repository.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception, naming the individual, what was missed and the risk impact.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry any unresolved exception into the next test cycle.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and draft the conclusion.
Have the Internal Auditor, independent of the assessment process, sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Configure real-time screening at new-business issuance
actions: Confirm the sanctions screening system is integrated via API with the Policy Administration Platform and Underwriting Platform so every new-business application triggers a screen before a policy can be issued.
Configure the screen to cover applicant, proposed insured, owner and any named beneficiary at intake.
Set the fuzzy-matching threshold per the vendor's tuning guide and validate against a test file of known SDN names.
checklist.done: the screening system is confirmed live on the issuance workflow with a validated matching threshold.

checklist.step: Screen the applicant, owner, insured and beneficiaries at intake
actions: In the Underwriting Platform, confirm the automated screening call fired and returned a result before advancing the application.
Where the automated call fails or times out, manually enter each party's full legal name and date of birth into the sanctions screening system and run the screen.
Do not release the application for underwriting decision until every party shows a Clear or Dispositioned-Clear result.
checklist.done: every party on the application shows a Clear or Dispositioned-Clear screening result before underwriting proceeds.

checklist.step: Disposition intake alerts
actions: Open each alert in the case queue and compare the matched SDN or sanctions-list entry's identifiers (date of birth, nationality, address, program) against the applicant's data.
Disposition as False Positive with documented rationale, or as a potential True Match requiring escalation.
For any potential true match, place the application on hold and notify the Financial Crime AML Officer the same business day.
checklist.done: every intake alert is dispositioned with documented rationale within 1 business day, and true-match candidates are held and escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Screen servicing transactions that change a party or payee
actions: In the Policy Administration Platform, confirm any beneficiary change, ownership change, address change to a high-risk jurisdiction, or added payee triggers an automated screening call.
Where the change is processed manually, submit the new/changed party to the sanctions screening system before completing the service transaction.
Hold the servicing transaction until the screening result returns Clear.
checklist.done: no servicing transaction that adds or changes a party completes without a Clear screening result on the new party.

checklist.step: Screen at claim and annuity payout
actions: In the Claims Platform, confirm the payee, claimant and any assignee is re-screened immediately before payment release, regardless of an earlier clean screen at issuance.
For structured settlements or annuity payouts, screen at each scheduled disbursement, not only at initiation.
Hold the payment in the Payment Gateway workflow until the payout screening result returns Clear.
checklist.done: every payout, including recurring annuity disbursements, carries a Clear screening result dated on or immediately before release.

checklist.step: Run daily batch rescreening against SDN List updates
actions: Confirm the sanctions screening system's data feed pulls the current OFAC SDN List, Consolidated List and any new sanctions program designation within 24 hours of OFAC publication.
Trigger the batch rescreen of the full in-force book of policyowners, insureds, beneficiaries and payees against the updated list.
Review the batch job completion log the next business day and confirm zero failed records.
checklist.done: the full in-force book is rescreened within 24 hours of every OFAC list update, with a clean batch completion log.

checklist.step: Investigate and disposition batch rescreen alerts
actions: Work each new alert from the batch rescreen using the same identifier-comparison method as intake alerts.
For any confirmed true match on an in-force policy, notify the Financial Crime AML Officer immediately and freeze any pending disbursement to that party.
Document the disposition and, for true matches, the blocking action taken.
checklist.done: every batch rescreen alert is dispositioned within 2 business days, with true matches immediately frozen from disbursement.

checklist.step: Escalate confirmed true matches for blocking or rejection
actions: On a confirmed true match, determine whether the applicable sanctions program requires blocking (property retained, reported to OFAC) or rejection (transaction refused, reported to OFAC).
Direct the Policy Administrator or Claims Processor to execute the block or rejection in the source system.
Hand off to the Corporate Secretary/General Counsel workflow to file the required OFAC report within 10 business days.
checklist.done: every confirmed true match has a documented block-or-reject determination executed in the source system, with the OFAC reporting workflow triggered.

checklist.step: Maintain the screening list configuration
actions: Confirm the screening system's list subscription includes the SDN List, Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List, Foreign Sanctions Evaders List and Consolidated Sanctions List.
Verify the vendor's list-update timestamp against the OFAC published update log monthly.
Escalate to the vendor immediately if a list update is missed or delayed beyond 24 hours.
checklist.done: the screening list subscription is confirmed complete and current against OFAC's own publication log.

checklist.step: Tune and validate the matching algorithm
actions: Run the quarterly false-positive/false-negative validation test using a seeded file of known matches and known non-matches.
Adjust the fuzzy-matching threshold if the false-negative rate exceeds the program's tolerance.
Document the validation result and any threshold change with rationale.
checklist.done: a quarterly matching-algorithm validation is documented with any threshold adjustment justified.

checklist.step: Log any exception where a transaction bypassed screening
actions: On discovery of an issuance, servicing or payout transaction that processed without a screening record, log it as a control exception immediately.
Determine whether the affected party is a true match by running a retrospective screen.
Escalate any retrospective true match to the Financial Crime AML Officer for OFAC self-disclosure assessment.
checklist.done: every bypass is logged, retrospectively screened, and any true match escalated for self-disclosure assessment.

checklist.step: Maintain the payment-hold protocol
actions: Confirm the Payment Gateway configuration prevents fund release while a screening alert on the payee remains open.
Periodically test the hold by simulating an open alert in a non-production environment and confirming payment cannot release.
Document the test result.
checklist.done: the payment-hold control is periodically tested and confirmed to block release while an alert is open.

checklist.step: Report screening program metrics monthly
actions: Compile monthly alert volume, disposition turnaround time, true-match count and any bypass exception for the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Feed the metrics into the quarterly Risk Committee board pack.
Flag any adverse trend (rising turnaround time, rising bypass rate) for management attention.
checklist.done: monthly screening metrics are compiled and any adverse trend flagged for management review.

checklist.step: Coordinate producer-level screening for distributed products

checklist.done: producer-submitted business is confirmed screened, with any bypass escalated for corrective action.

checklist.step: Retain screening evidence for the retention period

Apply the 5-year retention label to all screening logs and disposition notes.
Spot-check retrievability of a screening record by policy number.
checklist.done: screening evidence is retained for 5 years and retrievable by policy number.

Reconcile the extract count to the Payment Gateway's disbursement log for payout transactions.
Resolve any unreconciled difference before sampling.
testing.done: the transaction population is reconciled across source systems and the payment gateway.

testing.step: Reconcile the transaction population to the screening system's case log
actions: Match every population transaction to a corresponding screening case by transaction id and party name.
List any transaction with no matching screening case as an automatic exception — no judgement applied.
Compute the bypass rate for the month.

Take a random sample of 40 issuance and servicing transactions from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the screen for each sampled transaction

Compare the auditor's result to the recorded disposition without viewing the analyst's rationale first.

checklist.step: Triage the alert that may warrant a SAR
actions: Open the alert in NICE Actimize and confirm the alert type (structuring, unusual payment pattern, sanctions-adjacent activity, third-party payment).
Record the date of initial detection precisely — this date starts the 30-calendar-day filing clock, not the alert-review date.
Assign the case to the investigation queue and set the system-generated filing-deadline field.
checklist.done: the case is opened with the detection date correctly recorded and the 30-day filing clock running from that date.

checklist.step: Investigate the underlying activity
actions: Pull the policy, premium payment and beneficiary/payee history from the relevant source system (Policy Administration Platform or Claims Platform) for the party in question.
Interview the servicing team or claims handler who observed the activity, and document their account.
Cross-check the party against the sanctions screening system for any related alert history.
Draft the investigation narrative documenting the who, what, when, why and dollar amounts involved.
checklist.done: a complete investigation narrative with supporting transaction history and any related screening history exists.

checklist.step: Reach and document the filing decision
actions: Apply the SAR decision criteria from the procedure (known or suspected violation of law, no apparent lawful purpose, structuring pattern) to the investigation findings.
Draft a filing recommendation (File / Do Not File) with the reasoning.
Route the recommendation to the Financial Crime AML Officer for decision, with at least 10 calendar days remaining before the 30-day deadline.
checklist.done: a documented filing recommendation is routed to the Financial Crime AML Officer with adequate buffer before the deadline.

checklist.step: Approve the filing decision
actions: Review the investigation narrative and recommendation independently.
Confirm or overturn the recommendation and document the rationale.
Where overturned to 'Do Not File', document the specific reasoning in enough detail to withstand later examiner review.
checklist.done: a documented, dated approval or overturn of the filing recommendation exists from the Financial Crime AML Officer.

checklist.step: Complete the SAR form
actions: Complete FinCEN SAR Form 111 fields: filer information, subject information, suspicious activity information, and the narrative section summarizing the who/what/when/where/why.

Attach supporting transaction data as directed by the form instructions.
checklist.done: the SAR form is complete with a self-contained narrative and all required fields populated.

checklist.step: Submit the SAR through the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System
actions: Log in to the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System (bsaefiling.fincen.treas.gov) with the filing institution's registered credentials.
Upload or directly enter the completed SAR Form 111 and submit before the 30-calendar-day deadline (or 60 days if no subject was identified in time).
Retain the system-generated BSA ID / acknowledgment as proof of timely filing.
Do not notify the subject of the SAR filing under any circumstance, per the SAR confidentiality requirement.
checklist.done: the SAR is submitted through BSA E-Filing before its deadline with a retained acknowledgment, and no subject notification occurred.

checklist.step: File the SAR record in the evidence repository
actions: Upload the filed SAR, the BSA E-Filing acknowledgment and the investigation file to the compliance evidence repository, access-restricted per SAR confidentiality rules.

Close the NICE Actimize case with a link to the repository record.
checklist.done: the complete SAR record is filed, access-restricted, retention-labelled and the case closed.

checklist.done: every license-authorized transaction has its reporting conditions identified and calendared against the license's own deadline.

checklist.step: Prepare and submit any required license-condition report

Retain the submission confirmation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every license-condition report is submitted by its stated deadline with a retained confirmation.

checklist.step: Monitor the SAR filing clock across all open cases
actions: Run the weekly open-case aging report in NICE Actimize, sorted by days remaining to the filing deadline.
Escalate any case within 5 days of deadline with no completed investigation to the Financial Crime Investigator's manager.
Confirm no case is allowed to lapse past its deadline without a documented reason and General Counsel notification.
checklist.done: the weekly aging report is reviewed with any near-deadline case escalated before it lapses.

Route for the same approval and filing process as an initial SAR.
checklist.done: every continuing-activity SAR is filed within the 120-day cadence with an updated narrative.

Flag any decision that appears unsupported for reopening and reassessment.
testing.done: every sampled 'Do Not File' decision is independently reassessed for adequacy, with unsupported decisions flagged for reopening.

Confirm the underlying transaction was in fact within the license's scope and terms.
Flag any late report or any transaction found outside the license's stated scope.
testing.done: license-condition report timeliness and transaction scope-compliance is independently verified, with breaches flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception with the case id, what was missed and the regulatory impact.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date; for any late SAR, confirm a disclosure assessment is documented.
Carry every open exception into next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment, with late SARs tied to a documented disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references, maintaining SAR confidentiality in the report.

checklist.done: a current, merged employee-and-producer training-population list exists with new assignments flagged for the 30-day clock.

checklist.step: Refresh the training curriculum
actions: Update the curriculum content to reflect the current AML/sanctions program document, any new OFAC sanctions program designation, and lessons from the year's SAR/screening exceptions.
Include role-specific modules: underwriting/issuance screening duties, claims/payout screening duties, and producer-facing red-flag recognition.
Route the refreshed curriculum to General Counsel and the Learning & Development Specialist for review.
checklist.done: the refreshed curriculum with role-specific modules is reviewed by General Counsel and Learning & Development.

checklist.step: Build the training module in the LMS
actions: Load the refreshed curriculum content, including a scored knowledge-check assessment, into the learning management system.
Configure the module with a minimum pass score (e.g. 80%) and unlimited retake until passed.
Set the module's completion window at 30 days from assignment for new hires/producers and the annual recertification date for existing staff.
checklist.done: the training module is live in the LMS with a scored assessment and the correct completion window configured.

checklist.step: Assign the training to the covered population
actions: Bulk-assign the module to the full training-population master list in the LMS.
Confirm the automated 15-day and 25-day reminder notifications are enabled for each assignee.
For appointed producers not directly in the LMS, coordinate distribution through the agency/producer management system's compliance module.
checklist.done: the module is assigned to every individual on the master list with reminders enabled.

checklist.step: Monitor completion during the training window
actions: Pull the weekly completion-status report from the LMS.
Identify any assignee approaching the 25-day reminder without completion and confirm the reminder fired.
Coordinate directly with managers of employees still incomplete at day 28.
checklist.done: weekly completion monitoring is performed with direct manager follow-up for at-risk assignees before day 30.

checklist.step: Escalate and suspend access on non-completion
actions: On any assignee reaching day 30 without a passed completion, notify their manager (or the Producer Licensing Coordinator for producers) and the Head of Compliance.
Direct suspension of the individual's transaction-processing or new-business-writing access in the relevant system until training is completed.
Log the suspension in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: every non-completion past 30 days results in an access suspension and a logged tracker entry.

checklist.step: Reinstate access on cured completion
actions: Confirm the LMS shows a passed completion for the previously suspended individual.
Sign off reinstatement of transaction access.
Close the tracker entry with the cure date recorded.
checklist.done: access is reinstated only after confirmed completion, with sign-off and tracker closure documented.

checklist.step: Track producer-specific completion through licensing coordination
actions: Cross-reference the LMS/producer-portal completion report against the NIPR appointment roster monthly.
Flag any actively appointed producer without a current-year training completion.
Withhold new-business commission processing for flagged producers until training is confirmed complete.
checklist.done: producer training completion is cross-referenced to the appointment roster monthly, with commission processing withheld for non-compliant producers.

checklist.step: Verify role-specific content reaches the right audience
actions: Spot-check that claims-facing employees received the payout-screening module and underwriting-facing employees received the issuance-screening module, not a generic-only module.
Correct any misassignment in the LMS role mapping.
checklist.done: role-specific module assignment is spot-checked and any misassignment corrected.

checklist.step: Collect and act on assessment score data
actions: Pull the aggregate assessment score data by question to identify commonly missed concepts.
Where a concept is missed by more than 20% of takers, add supplemental guidance or a live briefing on that topic.
Document the analysis and any curriculum adjustment made.
checklist.done: assessment score data is analyzed and any weak concept addressed with supplemental content.

checklist.step: Deliver a live briefing for high-risk roles
actions: Schedule an annual live (or recorded live) briefing for the Sanctions Analyst, Financial Crime Investigator and Underwriting teams covering recent typologies and near-miss cases.
Record attendance in the LMS as a supplemental completion item.
Capture questions raised for potential curriculum updates.
checklist.done: a live annual briefing for high-risk roles is delivered with attendance recorded.

checklist.step: Report completion metrics to the Risk Committee
actions: Compile the final completion rate for employees and producers, average score, and any access-suspension count for the cycle.
Present as part of the standing quarterly/annual sanctions governance briefing.
Capture Committee feedback in the minute.
checklist.done: final completion metrics are reported to the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Log any training-process exception
actions: Log any process failure — module not assigned, reminder not sent, suspension not applied — as an exception with root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm the LMS configuration fix is applied.
Escalate any exception open beyond 30 days.
checklist.done: every training-process exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and escalation for overdue items.

checklist.step: Update the training procedure after any regulatory change
actions: Monitor OFAC guidance and NAIC producer-training model regulations for changes affecting the training obligation.
Redline the Annual OFAC/Sanctions Training Procedure accordingly.
Route to the Chief HR Officer for co-approval.
checklist.done: the training procedure reflects current OFAC/NAIC guidance with a current co-approval.

checklist.step: Retain training records for the retention period
actions: Export the full completion report, individual certificates and assessment scores from the LMS into the compliance evidence repository at cycle close.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Spot-check retrievability of an individual completion record by name.
checklist.done: the full cycle's training records are exported, retention-labelled and retrievable by individual name.

testing.step: Build the population of required trainees
actions: Independently pull the current HRIS roster for in-scope roles and the agency/producer management system's active-appointment roster.
Reconcile this independently-built population to the training-population master list used for assignment.
Flag any individual in the independent population missing from the assigned list.
testing.done: the population of required trainees is independently rebuilt and reconciled to the assigned list, with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Compute the overall completion rate
actions: Pull the LMS completion export for the full population and compute the completion rate by employee segment and by producer segment.
Compare to the prior cycle's rate and flag any material decline.
Identify every individual with no completion record at all.
testing.done: the completion rate is computed by segment with every non-completer identified.

testing.step: Select the sample of individual records
actions: Take 100% of individuals identified as never having completed the training.
Take a random sample of 25 completed records across employee and producer segments.
Record the population size, method and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all non-completers plus a random draw of completed records, documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Verify completion timing against the 30-day/annual standard
actions: For each sampled new-hire/newly-appointed record, compute days from assignment date to completion date and compare to the 30-day standard.
For each sampled existing-staff record, confirm completion occurred by the annual recertification date.
Flag any record exceeding the applicable standard.
testing.done: completion timing is independently verified against the applicable standard for every sampled record.

testing.step: Verify the assessment pass score
actions: For each sampled completed record, confirm the recorded assessment score meets or exceeds the minimum pass threshold.
Flag any record showing completion without a passing score.
testing.done: assessment pass scores are confirmed for every sampled completed record, or flagged.

testing.step: Verify access suspension for non-completers
actions: For each individual identified as a non-completer past 30 days, check the relevant system (Policy Administration Platform, agency/producer management system) to confirm transaction or new-business access was actually suspended.
Flag any non-completer found with active, unsuspended access.
testing.done: access suspension is independently confirmed for every non-completer past 30 days, or flagged as a control failure.

testing.step: Verify role-specific content assignment
actions: For a sample of 10 claims-facing and 10 underwriting-facing employees, confirm the LMS record shows the correct role-specific module assigned, not a generic-only module.
Flag any misassignment found.
testing.done: role-specific module assignment is independently spot-checked for a sample of high-risk roles.

testing.step: Confirm producer commission-hold enforcement
actions: For sampled non-compliant producers, confirm the billing/commission platform actually withheld commission processing during the non-completion period.
Flag any instance where commission was paid despite a non-completion flag.
testing.done: commission-hold enforcement is independently verified for sampled non-compliant producers, or flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception, naming the individual (or role) and the control impact.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry any unresolved exception into the next test cycle.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the final completion rate and exception count against the zero-tolerance threshold for past-30-day unsuspended access.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor, independent of training administration, sign the workpaper, then report to the Risk Committee and file in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and completion rate is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.
